items.title: Catherine Russell interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 26, 2018
items.q: Mom told me that they’d have bomb scares... underground railroad system of Miss Lulu’s is expecting certain bands

ctx.x: Like what kind of things might she have shared with you?

Well when she was with the International Sweethearts of Rhythm in the 40s, which was, there were several, probably many all-female bands and orchestras back then during World War II when all the men went overseas. But this orchestra started from a school, © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

from the Piney Woods School down south. And they really groomed their girls. And it was like the first interracial, multi-cultural female big band. And I’m not sure if there were others that were interracial. So when she came out of Juilliard she joined them for about a year and a half or so, and she would talk about traveling down south, which, the more biographies that I read of black artists in all genres, that was a, traveling down south you just didn’t know if you were going to make it — to the end of that…
